# A Greek-English Lexicon

Liddell, Henry George, and Robert Scott. *A Greek-English Lexicon*. Revised by Henry Stuart Jones with Roderick McKenzie. 9th ed. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1940. Selected LSJ entry transcriptions were read at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy’s CLD and Scaife ATLAS on 8 September 2026. Other dictionaries displayed on the same page retain separate authorship. Cite headword, sense and the actual transcription. Primary passages cited inside a lexicon are leads until independently collated.

The source **sources** lexical distinctions in [E2 Arbitration](../../../../etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md) and [E3 Fides–Credere](../../../../etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Those fields’ generated operations remain authorial register 3.

<a id="passages"></a>
## Selected lexical witnesses

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q001"></a>
### q001 — Topos

**Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes physical place, situated position, a passage in an author and a rhetorical topic. Aeschines 3.78 and Aristotle, Rhetoric 1358a14, are dictionary witnesses for distinct uses. These senses do not establish the authorial Arche-Topos compound or a mathematical theorem.

**Locator:** s.v. τόπος, place/position, textual passage and rhetorical topic.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/τόπος).

**Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q002"></a>
### q002 — Logos

**Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes reckoning, monetary accounts, account-giving, esteem, relation and mathematical ratio. Euclid V, definition 3, is cited for ratio. Their shared headword does not collapse their objects; the selected semantic range does not establish a complete philosophy of Logos.

**Locator:** s.v. λόγος, LSJ I.1–4 and II.1–2.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/λόγος).

**Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q003"></a>
### q003 — Nomos

**Paraphrase:** The entry associates νόμος with νέμω and distinguishes customary usage from law or ordinance. The differently accented νομός has its own entry. This is lexical evidence, not proof of a compulsory pasture-to-state history or of the essay’s sixfold.

**Locator:** s.v. νόμος, introduction and habitual practice/custom/law senses.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n71005/).

**Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q004"></a>
### q004 — Krisis

**Paraphrase:** The entry derives the noun from κρίνω and distinguishes separating, judging, choosing and judicial proceedings. Its Aristotle Politics 1275a23 citation connects judgment and office within the cited civic context. The dictionary is the verified witness here; that Aristotelian passage has not been independently collated for this card.

**Locator:** s.v. κρίσις, LSJ introductory and decision/judgment senses.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/κρίσις).

**Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q005"></a>
### q005 — Hybris

**Paraphrase:** The initial sense concerns overbearing violence and insolence; the Odyssey suitors supply several cited examples. The semantic witness is narrower than Taylor’s exact theorem of a local determination occupying its determining condition. That theorem retains authorial standing; the lexicon does not independently derive it.

**Locator:** s.v. ὕβρις, LSJ initial violence/insolence sense.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/ὕβρις).

**Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q006"></a>
### q006 — Anamnesis

**Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes calling to mind or recollection, reminders, a memorial sacrifice, and a separate lunar-return use. Its recollection citations include Plato, Phaedo 72e and 92d, Philebus 34c, and Aristotle, De memoria 451a21. These are dictionary witnesses; no complete Platonic argument is established by this card.

**Locator:** s.v. ἀνάμνησις, introductory recollection sense and senses 2–3.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n7019/).

**Verification:** entry read 2026-09-08; selected senses paraphrase-ready, ancient citation contexts and print edition not independently collated. **Consumer:** E2 recollection branch; the authorial return remains register 3.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q007"></a>
### q007 — Homologia

**Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes agreement and verbal consistency; assent, admission and concession; and compacts, including terms of peace or surrender. Plato, Symposium 187b and Theaetetus 164c, Aristotle, Topics 110a33, and the historical treaty citations are lexical witnesses here, not independently collated primary passages. The semantic range does not establish that every agreement is true, freely made or an instance of QL homology.

**Locator:** s.v. ὁμολογία, agreement, admission and compact senses, including the peace/truce/surrender sub-sense.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n73748/).

**Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 historical Greek branch and homological-agreement office; evidence register 2, with the authorial comparison at register 3.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q008"></a>
### q008 — Analogia

**Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes mathematical and general proportion, analogy including grammatical analogy, relation, and correspondence or resemblance. Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics 1131a31, is a dictionary locator for the equality-of-ratios sense; Plato, Timaeus 31c–32c, is another cited witness. These primary passages were not independently collated. The range does not identify proportional analogy, focal predication and qualified predication as one historical doctrine.

**Locator:** s.v. ἀναλογία, LSJ I–IV, including I.2 and II.2.

**Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n6926/).

**Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08 from the Scaife entry, retrieved via HTTP after the browsing tool's open error; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 analogy/Greek branches and C63's differentiated comparison grammars; evidence register 2, with the authorial coordination at register 3.

The agreement and proportion entries **source** [E5’s Greek historical branch](../../../../etymologies/homology-and-analogy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#e5-greek). The corresponding [whole-field](../../../../etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD.md) retains the project’s operational comparison at register 3.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q009"></a>
### q009 — Νέμω — distribution and holding a portion

**Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes distributing portions, assigning honour or privilege, and middle-voice holding as one’s portion. Examples concern meat, property and land. These are attested semantic offices; the dictionary citations are not independently collated primary passages and do not establish a single chronology from pasture to state.

**Locator:** s.v. νέμω, distributive active and possessive middle senses

**Verification:** s.v. νέμω, distributive active and possessive middle senses; https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.04.0057%3Aentry%3Dne%2Fmw ; read 2026-09-08, raw witness retained in T21-E6-private-development-packet.json. Paraphrase-ready to the online entry; print not collated. E6 branch E6-names consumes register-2 distribution/possession distinctions; its institutional return is register 3.

The entry **sources** [E6’s historical branch](../../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and its [whole-field](../../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md), with the institutional relation at register 3.

<a id="lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q010"></a>
### q010 — Symbolon — counterpart, guarantee and civic token

**Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes a token whose corresponding pieces enable subsequent recognition, a guarantee, and civic tokens used for entitlement or payment. Its listed ancient witnesses include Herodotus 6.86, Euripides Medea 613 and Plato Symposium 191d. Those citations identify different contexts; the dictionary supplies the verified semantic witness here.

**Locator:** s.v. σύμβολον, I.1, I.3 and I.5.

**Access:** [consulted online witness](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n98312/).

**Verification:** Selected online witness read on 2026-09-08 in the T21 E4 development; bounded finding and full-reading receipt retained in working/p2-enrichment/receipts/T21-etymology-symbol-account-and-trust-development.md and the historical companion. This admission reuses that completed consultation; no new retrieval, archived webpage, print collation or exact quotation is claimed.

**Use boundary:** Register 2, selected senses only. The cited ancient passages are not independently collated. Correspondence does not establish justice, future performance or a historical derivation of native QL.

The symbolon entry **sources** [E4’s token branch](../../../../etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#matching-tokens-and-institutional-recognition); [Symbol answering to source](../../../../etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/WHOLE-FIELD.md#symbol-answers-to-source) develops the authorial operation at register 3.
